headline: Reliance Communications enters Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process
sum: Reliance Communications Limited has filed for Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. The NSE disclosure on 20 Aug 2026 marks formal entry into the CIRP framework, opening the statutory 180-day (extendable to 270 days) resolution window.
implication: CIRP filing triggers mandatory disclosure obligations under IBBI rules; creditors must file claims within the prescribed period; the Insolvency Professional will assume control of the company's operations and pursue resolution/liquidation; key precedent in telecom sector M&A restructuring.
detail: Reliance Communications Limited, historically a major telecom operator in India, has formally entered the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process by filing before the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT). The company notified the NSE via disclosure letter on 20 Aug 2026. Under the IBC 2016, the debtor now enters a 180-day resolution window (extendable by up to 90 days) during which an Insolvency Professional is appointed to manage the company, a Committee of Creditors (CoC) is formed to evaluate resolution plans, and all creditors file claims. The process is designed to maximize asset recovery and determine whether the debtor should undergo resolution or be liquidated.

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC), Chapter II (Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process), Sections 4–37
framework.note: central: core statutory framework governing CIRP initiation, debtor duties, IP appointment, CoC formation, and creditor claims.

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) Regulations, 2016 (as amended)
framework.note: central: procedural rules for CIRP including disclosure norms, claim filing, CoC meetings, resolution plan evaluation, and timeline management.
central: CoC voting threshold (≥66% of voting share of creditors) required to approve any resolution plan.
central: constitution and powers of CoC; can reject resolution plans and trigger liquidation.

framework.ref: National Company Law Tribunal Rules, 2016 (NCLT Rules)
framework.note: central: tribunal procedures, appeal framework, admission of claims, and resolution plan hearings.

framework.ref: Indian Telecom Regulatory Authority (TRAI) Licensing Framework
framework.note: relevant: any resolution plan involving telecom license transfer/cancellation must comply with TRAI conditions and DoT/WPC approvals.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Regulations for Listed Companies / Stock Exchange Listing Rules
framework.note: relevant: continuous disclosure obligations for NSE/BSE listing; material event announcements required during CIRP.
relevant: if CoC rejects all resolution plans, debtor proceeds to liquidation under Liquidator; asset sale and creditor payout hierarchy apply.

conditions: 180-day resolution window (extendable to 270 days under IBC 2016, Section 12)
Appointment of Insolvency Professional by NCLT
Filing of creditor claims within prescribed moratorium period
CoC approval of resolution plan (≥66% voting share threshold)
NCLT approval of resolution plan or liquidation order
approvals: CoC approval of resolution plan (if any plan proposed)
NCLT approval of resolution plan or liquidation order
If telecom license involved: DoT/WPC clearance for license transfer or cancellation
structure.novel: High-profile telecom sector CIRP in India's insolvency framework; precedent for large-cap telecom operator restructuring under IBC 2016.

triggers.note: CIRP filed on default or on application by debtor/creditor; formal trigger is admission by NCLT.
Automatic moratorium on creditor suits and asset recovery; only IP/CoC can institute proceedings.

triggers.law: IBBI Regulations 2016, Part II (CIRP Procedural Rules)
triggers.note: IP disclosure, claim filing, information memorandum, resolution plan evaluation, CoC meeting rules.
If resolution plan involves telecom spectrum/license transfer, DoT and WPC consent required.
